clue.text: What adds something outstanding on tour of China?

definitions.text: What adds something outstanding on tour of China?

indicators.note: in an across answer, one thing 'on' another follows it, so the outstanding item comes after the China word

blocks.note: one who sums or adds up figures
rhyming slang: china plate = mate, i.e. pal
an ace is something first-rate

explanation.surface: A riddle about what adds something special to a sightseeing trip around China.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: the Summer Palace in Beijing is a standout stop on any China tour. 'China' for PAL is Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate).
explanation.definitionFit: The Summer Palace is a famous imperial garden complex in Beijing, a highlight of tourist itineraries.

clue.text: Suspect whose daughter is setting up diversion

indicators.note: something suspect is dodgy or not right, so these letters must be put into a new order
in a down answer, setting something up raises it so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
standard abbreviation for daughter
taken as written

explanation.surface: A detective wonders which suspect's daughter is staging a distraction.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged WHOSE, then D, then IS are written in a row and the whole string is flipped upwards to give SIDESHOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A sideshow is a minor attraction or distraction away from the main event, a diversion.

clue.text: So only the she-dog will bark?

definitions.text: So only the she-dog will bark?

blocks.clueFragment: So only the she-dog will bark?
blocks.note: surface reading: a situation where only female dogs make a noise
setter's reading: if the male is silent, only the female can bark; split the answer as two words to see this sled-dog breed

explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as MALE MUTE: with the dog silent, only the bitch barks. As one word it is a variant spelling of malamute, the Alaskan sled dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The malemute (or malamute) is a large Arctic sled-dog breed, so the clue's canine theme is the solution's category.

clue.text: Ronnie's (or Reggie's!) aunt has adopted one of the twins

indicators.note: to adopt is to take in, so the phrase before it holds the letters inside itself

blocks.note: surface padding: names the other Kray twin to set the scene
the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A remark about the Kray twins' aunt taking in a child.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronnie and Reggie Kray were notorious London gangster twins, which makes 'the twins' feel like them. The answer is the Biblical twin hidden in the words.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Esau and Jacob are the twin sons of Isaac and Rebekah.

clue.text: Aren't its components moving?

indicators.note: letters that are moving shift about, ending up in a different order

blocks.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about something whose parts are always in motion.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: the locomotives and carriages of a model railway are its moving components.
explanation.definitionFit: A train set is a toy railway whose engines and wagons run around the track.

clue.text: Diversion from suffering Maryland-Ohio trains

indicators.note: to train something is to direct or shape it, so these letters are guided into a new form

blocks.note: the two US state names, every letter used

explanation.surface: Rail services between two US states provide a distraction for someone in pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' looks like a noun for the railway, but it is a verb signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman holiday is entertainment derived from others' suffering, after the gladiatorial games.

clue.text: Flag of the Taoiseach perhaps finally taken down

indicators.note: the final element is removed, as a flag is lowered and taken off its pole

blocks.note: the Taoiseach is Ireland's prime minister, so an example of an Irish person

explanation.surface: An Irish leader's flag is lowered at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag' suggests a national banner, but it is the plant: a flag is another name for an iris.
explanation.definitionFit: Flag is a common name for the iris plant, especially the yellow water iris.

clue.text: Buried detail from censured nude won Surrealists over

indicators.note: a detail is a small section taken from a larger work, so the letters sit within the next words
turned over, so the run of letters is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: the letter run from the end of the first word to the start of the last

explanation.surface: Part of a censored nude painting won over the Surrealist movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Detail' sounds like art-history talk about a section of a painting, fitting the nude and Surrealists, but it marks the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be snowed under is to be overwhelmed or covered, as by work, i.e. buried.

clue.text: See 21
To see us shift 4 grand is so easy – invest pounds

indicators.note: as in 'take it easy' or loose, these letters are relaxed into a different arrangement
to invest is to put something inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: the nine letters to rearrange
L is the abbreviation for a pound (libra); doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: A salesperson boasts that selling a pricey item is easy money.
explanation.walkthrough: On a US keyboard, pressing Shift with 4 types $, so 'to see us shift 4' gets you dollar signs; the '4' is not a reference to 4-across here.
explanation.definitionFit: The $ symbol is typed with Shift plus the 4 key, so the character you see is the dollar sign.

clue.text: What's in pot – une pièce de résistance – in oven? I'm flexible

definitions.text: What's in pot – une pièce de résistance – in oven? I'm flexible

indicators.note: what sits inside a word is its central letter, so only the middle is kept
flexible letters bend into a different shape, so they are rearranged
the earlier pieces go inside the rearranged letters that follow

blocks.note: the central letter of the three
French for 'a piece of resistance': R is the symbol for electrical resistance
the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cook asks what's in the pot and the oven, and the diner says they'll eat any of it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: an eater who will take whatever is in the pot or oven. 'Pièce de résistance' looks like the showpiece dish, but here it is one letter of resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnivore eats both plant and animal food, so is flexible about whatever is served.

clue.text: Stuff removed from delicate projectile's path

blocks.note: to line, as in lining one's pockets, is to stuff or fill
taken off, removed
a light touch is a delicate one

explanation.surface: Packing material has been taken out of a fragile missile.
explanation.definitionFit: The line of flight is the course or trajectory along which something travels through the air.

clue.text: Not a specific problem for the audience

indicators.note: what is put on for listeners is heard rather than read, so the sound matters

blocks.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: A speaker addresses a vague issue to a room full of listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a specific' is an adjective phrase: 'some person' means an unspecified one.
explanation.definitionFit: Used before a noun, 'some' refers to an unidentified or unspecified one, as in 'some fool'.

clue.text: See 9
Restaurateur's offering to text us both

indicators.note: in text-message shorthand words are cut to single letters and joined up

blocks.note: one of us: me
'n' for 'and' plus 'u' for 'you' in text-speak, so the two of us together

explanation.surface: A restaurant owner offers to send a message to the two of us.
explanation.walkthrough: Written as a text, 'me and you' (i.e. both of us) becomes ME N U.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is the list of dishes a restaurant presents to diners.

clue.text: Constitution's beginning to help poorly baby set about taking exercise

indicators.note: something poorly is out of sorts, so these letters are out of order
to be set about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps the rest
the rearranged letters take in the exercise abbreviation

blocks.note: wee is Scottish for tiny
the six letters to rearrange
physical education

explanation.surface: A sick baby is helped by being given some exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitution' suggests health, fitting the poorly baby, but it is the US Constitution, whose preamble opens with these words.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States Constitution begins with the phrase 'We the People of the United States'.

clue.text: See 7
Silly not coming to me following emotional blow?

indicators.note: silly means foolish or nonsensical, so these letters are put in a jumbled order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
heading this way, i.e. bound for here

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly refuses an approach after being emotionally hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' looks like part of the sentence's sense but only rearranges the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on the rebound is to be reacting to the end of a relationship, i.e. just after an emotional blow.

clue.text: Drab farfalle's plated up with basil

indicators.note: served up, which in a down answer lifts the letters so they read bottom to top

blocks.note: the closing four letters of the pasta name
the opening four letters of the herb

explanation.surface: A dull plate of bow-tie pasta is served garnished with basil.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is uncertain: the end of the pasta name and the start of the herb, read upwards. Keats's poem 'Isabella, or the Pot of Basil' gives the basil a second point.
explanation.definitionFit: Isabella is a greyish-yellow or dun colour, so a drab shade.

clue.text: Where the privileged learn nothing: Times cryptic grid filling live!

indicators.note: something cryptic is obscure or puzzling, so these letters are disguised by rearrangement
a filling sits inside, so the rearranged letters go within the next word

blocks.note: zero, nought
the multiplication sign
to be is to exist, to live
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A snipe that the elite learn nothing from the Times crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times cryptic grid' reads as the newspaper's puzzle, but Times is a multiplication sign and cryptic rearranges the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Oxbridge, the blend of Oxford and Cambridge, stands for the elite universities associated with privilege.

clue.text: Women, it was said, wrongly taking time off with jilted partner of broadcaster

indicators.note: the abbreviation for time is taken away from the word before

blocks.note: taking wrongfully is stealing
a broadcaster is one who airs things; his or her jilted partner is an ex

explanation.surface: A broadcaster's dumped partner says she was wrongly accused about women and took time off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It was said' marks the phrase as old-fashioned usage rather than a sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: 'The fairer sex' is a dated, patronising expression for women.

clue.text: Barbarian now found in new health unit

indicators.note: something new is made afresh, so these letters are formed into a different order

blocks.note: as in 'at home' for 'in the house'
the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A thug has turned up at a newly opened clinic.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila, leader of the Huns, ravaged the Roman Empire and is the archetypal barbarian.

clue.text: See 15
One directing spies to track the US? No!

indicators.note: to track is to follow behind, so this piece comes after the next one

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the head of the Secret Service in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A spymaster asks whether to follow the United States, then refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The US' reads as America, but the definition is the pronoun 'us', rejected in favour of its opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: If it is not us, it is them: the third-person pronoun contrasted with the first person.

clue.text: Having nipped back, batter well done?

definitions.text: Having nipped back, batter well done?

blocks.note: surface reading: cooking, with a mixture of batter baked thoroughly
setter's reading: cricket, where a ball that darts back off the pitch beats the batsman and hits the stumps

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a ball 'nips back' when it deviates off the seam; the batter is then out with the stumps hit directly. 'Well done' is also a nod to a cook's bowl scraped clean.
explanation.definitionFit: A batsman is out this way when the bowled ball hits the wicket without touching bat or pad.

clue.text: Archbishop's appendage carried back to front

indicators.note: the letter at the back is moved round to the front of the word

blocks.note: past tense of bear, to carry

explanation.surface: A clerical accessory was carried the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appendage' is the signature appended to the Archbishop of York's name, from the Latin Eboracum for York.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebor is the signature used by the Archbishop of York, added after his first name.

clue.text: Concern for horse-breeding boss

blocks.note: first meaning: a business where horses are bred
second meaning: a raised knob or ... on a surface

explanation.walkthrough: 'Concern' means a business here, and 'boss' is the ornamental knob, not the manager.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is an establishment for breeding horses, and also a projecting knob, as a boss on a shield.

clue.text: Part of suite yet to be completed

indicators.note: something still to be completed is unfinished, so the last letter is missing

blocks.note: 'yet' as in 'up to now'

explanation.surface: A furniture order that has not yet been finished.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-piece suite consists of a settee plus two armchairs, so the settee is one part.

clue.text: The writer's favourite work receives a single complaint

indicators.note: to receive is to take in, so a letter is held within the pair before it

blocks.note: the writer is the setter: I am
a teacher's pet is a favourite
as a machine goes, i.e. works
the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An author's best-loved book attracts one critical review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' looks like a grumble about the work, but it is an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetigo is a contagious skin infection, and complaint is a standard word for an illness.

clue.text: See 24
Something I'll wager will embellish social event in the City?

definitions.text: Something I'll wager will embellish social event in the City?

indicators.note: embellishing adds decoration around something, so the stake wraps the next pieces

blocks.note: the stake put up before a poker hand
EC is the postal district of the City of London
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A gambler bets that a story will get exaggerated at a City party.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a tale told at a City drinks party is bound to be embellished. 'In the City' places a party within London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing story, the kind that gets embellished with each retelling.

clue.text: See 1
